topic: Default Member Initializers in Structs and Classes
explanation: In modern C++, default member initializers allow developers to specify initial values for class or struct members directly at their point of declaration. This feature simplifies constructor definitions by providing default values, enhances code readability, and reduces boilerplate. It is particularly useful for setting sensible defaults and ensuring members are initialized consistently across multiple constructors, promoting safer and more maintainable code.
example_explanation: This example demonstrates how default member initializers set initial values for members 'a' and 'b' in the struct 'B2'. When creating 'obj1' with the default constructor, 'a' and 'b' are initialized to 13 and 42 respectively, thanks to the default member initializers. For 'obj2', the constructor explicitly overrides these defaults. This showcases how default member initializers simplify object initialization and improve code clarity in modern C++.
